segments.text: Welcome to your daily AI news digest from October 25th, 2026.
We've got 35 stories today, including deep dives into world model architectures, multi-agent systems, and new cybersecurity agent plugins.
Tune in for the updates.
From turingpost.com, "World Model Architectures: How AI Predicts the World".

This report details how artificial intelligence captures the dynamics of the world through world models, which are systems that learn the rules governing how the world changes to enable the prediction of future states based on current observations and actions.

The research explores various architectural categories including generated observations, compact latent states, and explicit object structures, employing methods such as Visual-token models, Diffusion and flow models, and representation learning via JEPA.
These models facilitate rendering, simulation, and planning by internalizing underlying physics and spatial relationships.
The development focuses on learning the rules of world dynamics to facilitate advanced predictive capabilities.
Progress in this area points toward more sophisticated AI systems capable of complex environmental simulation and planning.
From MarkTechPost, "Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents".

This report details the open-sourcing of Agensh, a decentralized multi-agent harness that enables coding agents to coordinate without a central orchestrator, demonstrating significant performance gains in complex task completion.
The system facilitates autonomous coordination where workers select sub-tasks, share findings, and merge code into a common Git repository utilizing services such as Gitea and Mattermost.

Scaling the setup to one thousand twenty-four agents on ProgramBench resulted in an improvement in the mean task-pass rate from nineteen point three one percent to twenty-eight point seven eight percent with one hundred twenty-eight agents.
The cooperative loop involves concurrent steps of gathering context, claiming tasks, taking action, verifying results, and merging progress.
Furthermore, the system achieved a seventy-nine point five nine percent performance on pandoc with GPT-6.1-sol when tested with thirty-two agents.
This development indicates a pathway for more robust, decentralized coordination in large-scale artificial intelligence workflows.
From MarkTechPost, Cognition open-sourced an agent plugin that assists in securing systems against recent cybersecurity threats.
This release introduces a set of agent skills designed to mitigate vulnerabilities in PHP, Node.js, and GitLab, specifically addressing critical remote code execution issues.
The process involves an inventory of vulnerabilities, an approval gate, thorough testing, and the generation of a single pull request per repository.
This methodology operates across various coding agents and necessitates access to tools such as git, a shell, and Docker, emphasizing a safe workflow through validation prior to any modifications.
This development indicates a push toward integrating verifiable security checks directly into automated software development processes.
Further developments in agent-based security tools are anticipated.
From Towards Data Science, "How to Add Guardrails to a Local LLM Agent"
details methods for implementing runtime control in local large language model agents through guardrails, demonstrating the ability to validate inputs or outputs before execution.
The study explored placing these guardrails at various points of the agentic process, including input, tool-input, tool-output, and final output checks.
A specific case study involved implementing a tool-output guardrail to redact sensitive internal data present in tool results prior to agent processing.
This technique successfully prevented the agent from exposing private information to a customer while retaining the necessary contextual details.
The selection of the appropriate guardrail depends on the desired control over the request, tool calls, data returns, or the final response.
This work indicates a growing necessity for robust safety mechanisms within local agent systems.
Further development in agentic safety protocols is anticipated.
From MarkTechPost, "How to Run Underdog Saluki 27B: 2-Bit Qwen3.8-27B Tool-Calling Guide"
details the method for running the Underdog Saluki 27B model, which preserves tool-calling capabilities with only two bits per weight.

The analysis of the GGUF headers reveals that the Saluki model involved changing the data types of one hundred forty-six tensors, predominantly affecting the feed-forward down projections and output layers.

Byte-level provenance indicated that the majority of unchanged-type tensors were byte-identical to the ISTA model, confirming that the Saluki modification constitutes a subtle alteration rather than a simple re-encoding of the original file.
This investigation provides insight into efficient model modifications and quantization techniques within the current AI landscape.
From The Decoder, Nvidia open-sourced Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra.
This report details the release of Flora, an open data engine designed to significantly reduce the cost of labeling video data for robot learning applications.
Flora achieves this by processing video to generate the three required labels for robot learning: action descriptions, step-by-step progress ratings, and task success judgments.
The methodology involves breaking videos into segments and employing fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models for segmentation, captioning, and reward evaluation.
Testing estimates the labeling cost for one hour of video using Flora at seventy-two cents, in contrast to approximately eighty-eight dollars and fifty cents for GPT-6 Astra.
Flora demonstrated superiority in providing fine-grained temporal localization and error detection within robot video datasets.
This development suggests a pathway toward more cost-effective and precise training data generation for embodied artificial intelligence systems.
From The Decoder, Anthropic says one AI agent beats many subagents now that models can handle complexity alone.

This report details a recommendation by Anthropic advocating for the consolidation of specialized sub-agents into a single AI agent that loads context on demand, noting that this approach frequently surpasses multi-agent setups regarding quality, cost, and latency.
Experience gathered indicates that sequential multi-agent handoffs introduce context loss and increased delays.
Newer large models demonstrate the capability to manage complex planning internally, thereby diminishing the necessity for numerous separate agents.
Anthropic has provided a migration kit to assist teams in transitioning to this unified agent architecture.
This shift indicates a potential trend toward centralized, context-aware AI agents for complex tasks.
From substack.com, "[2610.30468] SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research".
This report details an autonomous research system designed for 3D Gaussian Splatting research that automates hypothesis drafting and code writing to accelerate scientific discovery.
The SplatLab system reproduces baseline papers, proposes extensions, and trains models utilizing Mip-NeRF 360 and LLFF.

The system incorporates five design choices, including an Elo tournament and a standing falsifier, to select and validate research candidates, compressing the research cycle from months to days and achieving superior results in tasks such as astrophotographic nebula rendering.
This advancement suggests a significant acceleration in the pace of 3DGS research and the potential for automated scientific exploration.
From RL Reddit, "Verifiable-reward problems from an open research area: solved rungs for training, open rungs with exact success criteria".

This story details the creation of AI puzzles based on aperiodic order research to explore verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning, with the key finding being the development of a nine-rung ladder of puzzles ranging from human to artificial superintelligence levels.
The author constructed a set of puzzles utilizing concepts from aperiodic order theory, designed to be solved using verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning.

Some of these puzzles allowed for solved rungs with exact answers providing straightforward rewards, while others featured open rungs defined by precise success criteria, certificates, and numerical evidence, where solving them constituted a potential research result.
This structure forms a ladder of nine items across varying levels of difficulty.
This work indicates a methodology for structuring complex AI challenges with measurable success criteria for advanced training.
From substack.com, "[2610.22791] Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization".

This report details a recursive framework that optimizes large language model agents by iteratively refining both the policy model and the harness mediating environment interaction, demonstrating superior performance across coding benchmarks.

The methodology involves a self-HPO process where the evolving policy proposes new harness candidates based on observed failures, and the policy is then updated through reinforcement learning under the selected harness.

This iterative optimization process consistently yields better results than approaches optimizing only the harness or only the policy, significantly increasing the agent's resolve rate and capability frontier through synergistic gains.
This development indicates a pathway for creating more robust and capable AI coding agents through integrated system optimization.
From RL Reddit, "I trained a PPO agent to farm the Pit in D2R".
This report details the training of a Proximal Policy Optimization agent to automate farming within the game D2R.
The resulting model possesses approximately four hundred seventy-five thousand parameters.
The training process was conducted offline within a custom Rust-based headless simulation utilizing a single CPU over a duration of approximately twenty minutes.

The reward function incorporated a negative reward per second, positive rewards for kills and item values, and a significant penalty for death, with an initial level clear bonus subsequently removed from the system.
This methodology demonstrates the application of reinforcement learning to complex, simulated environments.
Future research may explore the scalability of such agent training methods across more complex game mechanics.
From RL Reddit, "RL agents play World of Warcraft 3v3 arena".

This story details the training of reinforcement learning agents to play a three versus three setup in a World of Warcraft arena, with the agents successfully learning a specific tactic to eliminate a healer by immediately interrupting casts.
The learning process involved mastering crowd control, trinket usage, ice block, and various cooldown abilities within the simulated environment.
Each agent was trained independently utilizing the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm, replicating game logic from AzerothCore 3.3.5a.
This autonomous behavior demonstrates the capacity of artificial intelligence to develop complex, context-specific strategies in complex simulated environments.
Future developments in reinforcement learning suggest increasing potential for artificial intelligence in strategic gameplay and decision-making systems.
From RL Reddit, "AI Beats the Human World Record on One of the Hardest Surf Maps".
This report details how a reinforcement learning agent successfully completed a difficult surf map faster than the established human world record.
The agent achieved this feat by operating within an optimized simulation that incorporated Counter-Strike 1.6 movement logic.
The algorithm employed a Proximal Policy Optimization method augmented with an AlphaZero-style expert loop for further refinement during training.
Camera movements were smoothed to facilitate tracking of A/D inputs while obscuring high-frequency micro-strafing.
This demonstrates an artificial intelligence capacity to execute complex physical movements surpassing known human performance limits in simulated environments.
Future developments in reinforcement learning are expected to continue exploring these boundaries.
From The Decoder, Block's new AI model Dessa was trained entirely on human speech to catch emotions text-based models miss.
This report details the development of Dessa, an artificial intelligence model designed to perceive emotional nuances directly from audio.
The model processes speech in real time to detect emotions, sarcasm, laughter, and pauses, a capability that text-based models currently lack.
Dessa supports full-duplex communication and operates locally on hardware such as the MacBook Pro M4 Max.
This development was undertaken by Block with the stated objective of addressing safety concerns and enhancing human-AI communication through the incorporation of emotional cues.
Researchers are currently seeking AI security experts to evaluate the model for potential risks.
The focus shifts toward the integration of affective computing into future artificial intelligence systems.
From TechCrunch - AI, "The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it".

This report details a running list of AI projects and startups that have failed or been abandoned, revealing that approximately forty-two percent of AI initiatives are dropped by their corporate parents due to factors such as funding issues or competition.
Notable examples include the shutdowns of workflow tool Relay and the chatbot platform Character.ai, both of which filed for bankruptcy following legal and regulatory challenges.
Furthermore, major entities like OpenAI have discontinued standalone tools such as ChatGPT Atlas and Sora owing to operational or user challenges.
Hardware ventures, including Humane AI Pin and Rabbit R1, have also demonstrated significant struggles in the development space.
These failures underscore the inherent risks present within the current artificial intelligence development landscape.
The data suggests that significant attrition is occurring across the sector, emphasizing the critical need for robust operational strategies in future technological advancements.
From TechCrunch - AI, "Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages".

This report details several artificial intelligence agents capable of performing various tasks directly through text messaging, demonstrating the potential for seamless integration of AI into daily communication.
These agents include Ask Proxy, which anticipates needs, Caddy, which organizes information from messages, and Fambot, a family assistant coordinating household tasks.
Additional agents such as Instinct, Folk, and Rene focus on personal assistance, while Wajo possesses the capability to interact with businesses on behalf of users.
These systems illustrate the ability to embed sophisticated AI functionality directly within standard messaging platforms for scheduling, research, and coordination.
This development points toward a future where AI assistants operate as inherent parts of communication streams across numerous life functions.
From The Verge - AI, Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads.
This report details the enactment of the AI Deceptive Advertising Act, which mandates labeling for advertisements significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence within the state.
The law extends this requirement to various ad formats including commercials and flyers.
The legislation establishes that disclosures are necessary only when the synthetic content creates a false consumer perception regarding a product or service.
The specific criteria for what constitutes significantly modified or evidently fictional content remain subjective and are currently undefined within the statute.
This state represents an early application of mandatory disclosures for artificial intelligence generated content in advertising.
The industry must now address the ambiguity surrounding these definitions to ensure compliance with the new state regulation.
From The Verge - AI, "Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI".
This report details how the BBC's Blue Planet III incorporated less-than-perfect footage to demonstrate authenticity in the age of artificial intelligence.
The production deliberately included shots of plankton and natural imperfections that would typically be omitted to counter the perception of artificial perfection in the series.

This approach allowed the program to showcase authentic ocean scenes, such as dolphins trapping fish and complex crab formations, emphasizing that real ocean life is more remarkable than what artificial generation can produce.
This methodology prioritized visual veracity over flawless rendering in the context of AI-generated media.
The decision suggests a trend toward valuing raw, unpolished reality in high-production content.
From thehustle.co, Williams-Sonoma furnished a comeback without homebuyers.

This report details how the company achieved a significant stock increase over three years despite a slow housing market by capitalizing on a customer base more insulated from economic strains and a greater willingness to spend on home furnishings.
Williams-Sonoma also effectively leveraged its business-to-business revenue stream, which saw a fourteen point five percent growth in the second quarter of twenty twenty six.
The company is currently expanding into new markets including cruise ships, senior living, and student housing, creating a balanced operational structure across consumer and business segments.
This strategic realignment demonstrates adaptability in response to evolving economic conditions.
The movement suggests a trend of diversified revenue streams in retail sectors.
From The Rundown AI, "SAP's Philipp Herzig on AI built for business data"
reports on SAP's perspective regarding the development of enterprise artificial intelligence.

Philipp Herzig argues that the notion that Software as a Service is obsolete fails to account for the complexity of operating businesses built upon applications, emphasizing that successful enterprise AI necessitates robust business context, governance, and security alongside application development.
To achieve accuracy, SAP employs Knowledge Graphs to map business data and captures historical decision rationales through a system called Company Memory.
Tokenomics is utilized to optimize AI utilization by prioritizing cost-effective business outcomes instead of solely deploying the most advanced models.
Furthermore, Tabular AI provides specialized tools for structured data, enabling explainable predictions such as payment delays.
This approach signals a shift toward contextually grounded and governed AI implementation across the enterprise sector.
From The Decoder, OpenMobile-2 proves open-source smartphone agents can rival proprietary models.
This report details research demonstrating that open-source smartphone agents can achieve competitive performance against proprietary models.
The project involved training smartphone agents using a simulated environment encompassing over one hundred applications, including services such as Taobao and Google Drive.

Success in training was found to be more dependent on the diversity of applications trained on rather than the sheer volume of data, as increasing the number of trained applications led to improved success rates.

The larger model within the OpenMobile-2 family achieved a score of 59.6 points on the SPA-Bench benchmark utilizing real Android devices, emphasizing the role of comprehensive training diversity and direct application commands in enhancing agent performance.
This research suggests a pathway for open-source models to advance in capability.
From TechCrunch - AI, "Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats."
This report examines the differential political leaning observed between two large language models when forced to select candidates in an election scenario.

A study conducted revealed that when prompted to choose in midterm elections, the Grok model recommended Republicans in ninety-two percent of instances, whereas the OpenAI model's GPT recommended Democrats in ninety-seven percent.
Researchers suggest that these differences indicate implicit biases present within the AI models, which are reflected in their search patterns and the sources they prioritize.
The study further indicated a notable divergence between the behavior of these models when used in consumer applications versus when accessed through application programming interfaces.
These findings point to the influence of underlying data and information prioritization on the models' outputs.
This research signals a need for scrutiny regarding the potential for large language models to subtly shape political perspectives.
From The Decoder, Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt calls OpenAI and Anthropic modern colonial trading companies.
This segment explores the observation that the concentration of artificial intelligence resources suggests a colonial economic dynamic between major powers.

Schmidt posits that the United States and China are engaging in mirrored strategies concerning artificial intelligence development, specifically through the deployment of closed systems versus open-weight models, which generates global dependency.
This competition is complicated by control over Taiwan and the AI supply chain, which is constrained by access to energy, minerals, and semiconductors.
Both powers are confronted by fiscal limitations, presenting an imperial trilemma involving defense, technological leadership, and welfare expenditures.
The authors propose an AI détente, analogous to the Cold War, for risk management.
This dynamic necessitates attention to the emerging geopolitical and supply chain tensions within the artificial intelligence sector.
From The Decoder, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark moves his prediction for self-improving AI forward to 2027.
This report details a revision of the timeline for recursive self-improvement in artificial intelligence, moving the predicted arrival date from 2028 to 2027.

A new benchmark named TasteVal was introduced to measure how effectively AI systems can design experiments and interpret outcomes, demonstrating a steep improvement curve in this capability known as research taste.
Reports indicate that this research taste has reportedly doubled every three months since December of 2025.

This metric emphasizes the model's ability to select research trajectories and guide experimental procedures, moving the focus from raw performance metrics to the efficacy of the AI in scientific exploration.
This development prompts examination of the anticipated pace and verification methods for AI-driven scientific progress.
Industry observers should monitor the trajectory of this research advancement closely.

From AI Alignment Forum, Setting the Scene Public version one October twenty-fifth highlights significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities and the necessity for AI safety considerations amid rapid advancements in large language models.
A recent incident involving an OpenAI model on the Hugging Face platform illustrated potential risks concerning agent behavior and overall system security.

Experts indicate that the current velocity of artificial intelligence development is exceeding the capacity for understanding and control of these systems, generating concerns regarding the possibility of rogue artificial intelligence and a subsequent loss of control.
A call has been made for international collaboration to pace the frontier by developing requisite technical and governance instruments.
This discussion underscores the requirement for serious evaluation of the security and societal consequences associated with increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems.
The industry must prioritize the development of robust safety protocols and governance frameworks moving forward.
From The Decoder, "AI makes junior patent attorneys instantly better but may quietly stunt their professional growth".
This report examines the impact of artificial intelligence assistance on the performance and professional development of junior patent attorneys.
The study found that AI assistance immediately improved junior attorneys' performance in drafting tasks, resulting in enhanced scores in enforceability and accuracy.
The research involved assessing junior patent attorneys' performance across various drafting tasks with and without AI support, alongside evaluations of their judgment in critical review scenarios.

The findings indicated that while AI accelerated immediate output, the benefits were not uniformly distributed, with some junior attorneys showing reduced growth in expertise during critical review tasks when their judgment was assessed independently.
This research suggests that baseline expertise is necessary for AI assistance to translate into durable professional skill.
The findings contribute to considerations regarding the potential stagnation of professional expertise due to reliance on artificial intelligence tools.
From Interconnects, "Podcast: Kimi K3.1 Pro, the new cyber reality, and Muse musings"
examines the trade-offs in recent artificial intelligence developments focusing on the Kimi K3.1 Pro release and open-weight models.
Nathan and Florian discussed the implications of model benchmarks and the professionalization of model launches.

The conversation addressed the risks associated with open-weight models and cybersecurity, exploring the relationship between offensive capabilities and defensive measures, including the role of nation-states.
A central concern raised involved the discrepancy between public apprehension regarding AI capabilities and the observable mass exploitation of existing vulnerabilities.
This discussion highlights the necessity for robust security protocols surrounding advanced model deployments.
Future developments in AI will require intensified focus on integrated security and defensive frameworks.
From RL Reddit, "CUDA-Accelerated Rocket League - Full Write-up"

details the development and benchmarking of a GPU-resident Rocket League simulator, CARL, which demonstrated significant speedups in data collection and update-adjusted throughput using current-generation graphics processing units.
The research involved creating a simulator resident on a GPU and comparing its performance against the RLGymPPO_CPP environment.
The results indicated that training speed improvements reached nine to ten times faster on an RTX 3060 and up to fifty times faster on an RTX 5090.
This acceleration allows for the reduction of extensive experiment times from a full day to a few hours and a month-long run to a couple of days.
This acceleration has major implications for the efficient testing of numerous algorithms and configurations in machine learning applications.
From thehustle.co, "Subscribe to The Hustle Daily Newsletter - The Hustle"
details content covering diverse topics ranging from forensic pathology in Iceland to the evolution of barcodes and the future of artificial intelligence.
The platform presents in-depth investigative pieces and trending consumer interests across financial history, technology, and branding.
Stories explored the impact of tiny logos and the history of billion-dollar company names alongside consumer trends like the rise of carnivorous plants and romance bookstores.
Free resources are also provided to assist readers in finding side hustle ideas.
This continuous presentation mixes complex investigative material with current consumer fascinations.
The focus on technology and branding suggests continuous evolution within the digital economy.
From Towards Data Science, "Python 3.15 Has a New Profiler"
reports on the introduction of two new built-in profiling tools in Python 3.15, focusing on deterministic tracing and process sampling.

The new tools include profiling.tracing, which provides exact call counts similar to cProfile, and profiling.sampling, which allows for the inspection of running processes by sampling call stacks, CPU work versus waiting, and global interpreter lock usage.

Demonstrations show these tools can be utilized on an HTTP server to differentiate time allocated to computation from time spent waiting, offering estimates rather than exact counts for sampling methods.
The existing cProfile module remains accessible for exact call count requirements.
This update provides advanced methods for performance analysis within Python applications for developers in the AI and technology sectors.
From 🔳 Turing Post, "LeHami Explained – Can Physics Help World Models Predict Motion?".
This story details a physics-inspired joint embedding predictive autoregressive model that incorporates Hamiltonian mechanics to stabilize long-term latent predictions.
The research introduces LeHami, a world model that represents states using position-like and momentum-like variables and learns an energy-like function to prevent collapse.
The state updates are performed using a symplectic leapfrog integrator, a method borrowed directly from Hamiltonian mechanics.
Experiments conducted on simulated pendulums demonstrated promise regarding prediction accuracy and efficiency in this framework.
Planning results remain mixed, and the method has not yet been applied to complex, real-world dynamics.
Future research will focus on extending these findings to more intricate physical systems.
From The Decoder, "OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers".
This report details how OpenAI has utilized aggressive pricing strategies to attract major enterprise customers from Anthropic, resulting in a significant shift in spending patterns.
Companies such as Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp have accepted substantial price reductions from OpenAI.
Specific examples include over thirty percent discounts offered to Replit and cost reductions ranging from eighty to ninety percent for DataCamp.
This cost reduction has been facilitated by the deployment of more efficient models, including Sol and Luna, by OpenAI.
Both organizations are concurrently experiencing increased pricing pressure from competitors operating in the Chinese market.
This trend signals intensified competitive dynamics within the artificial intelligence sector.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "‘Synthetic twin’: Why Socceroo Cristian Volpato is the latest footballer to license his AI clone".
This story concerns a footballer licensing his artificial intelligence likeness to create synthetic images, marking him as the latest athlete to monetize their digital identity.
Cristian Volpato has licensed his AI likeness to Callandor to generate synthetic images.

This process involves the creation of digital likenesses, voice, and performance data, with the company Callandor aiming to utilize these synthetic twins for brand engagements and potential applications such as real-time football instruction.

Athletes are currently seeking to establish rights over these digital assets before widespread technology deployment, which raises questions regarding consent and the distinction between authentic and fabricated content.
Legal analysis indicates that existing copyright frameworks present challenges in addressing AI reproductions and intellectual property rights.
The development signals an evolving legal and commercial landscape for digital athlete identities and intellectual property in the context of artificial intelligence.
From thehustle.co, "Romance bookstores are having a meet-cute moment".

This report details the significant resurgence of the romance bookstore movement, driven by online shopping and social media trends such as BookTok, resulting in the opening of over two hundred thirty romance bookstores globally in the last three years.
Print book sales within the romance genre more than doubled between two thousand twenty and two thousand twenty-three, ultimately reaching thirty-nine million units sold in two thousand twenty-three.
This genre has established itself as a top-grossing category, generating substantial revenue through curated, judgment-free environments offering diverse romance subgenres.
The increased commercial success of romance fiction indicates a growing market for emotionally driven narrative content in the publishing sector.
Further analysis of consumer engagement with digital storytelling will provide insight into future market shifts.
From The Decoder, "Three fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were never told what they actually leaked".

This report details a dispute involving three former OpenAI safety researchers who deny sharing confidential information, suspecting their termination related to advocating for improved AI monitoring.
The conflict arose from an internal investigation triggered by suspicions that details regarding the company's internal model architecture were shared with an external researcher.
The dispute centered on the debate concerning whether AI companies should permit external inspection of their models' reasoning steps.
OpenAI stated the terminations were unrelated to the safety concerns raised, yet the researchers maintain they were never informed of the information they allegedly disclosed.
This incident introduces new considerations regarding internal reporting of safety concerns within the artificial intelligence sector.
And that's all the neural net news for today, October 25th, 2026.
Keep pondering those world models, and I'll catch you in the next byte.
Bye for now!
